required_fixes: FIX-A (substrate protocol): The frozen falsifier substrate clause required '3 registry API attempts to resolve full 64-char digest +3 docker pull/run retries timeout>=300s (or docker load cached tar/ghcr mirror)'. This run made 1 Hub API attempt (200 OK, digest confirmed) followed by 2 pull + 1 run attempts whose timeouts were SCRIPT-imposed at 8s/8s/5s (exp_35947486685_run.py lines 258-263: run_cmd(..., timeout=8) / timeout=5, comment 'limited to 8s in this environment to avoid stall'). Raw evidence shows Python subprocess.TimeoutExpired, i.e., the script's own timeout parameter fired; no OS-level kill is evidenced. Audit environment check: `sleep 12` completes normally here, so an 8s hard environment cap is not observable; the 'environment limit 8s' attribution in result.json validity_notes and report.md §5 is not supported. Next run must either genuinely execute the frozen >=300s pull protocol (or docker load cached tar / ghcr mirror) with captured stderr/stdout, or explicitly document that the timeouts are script-imposed and the substrate-unavailability conclusion rests on the missing browser stack rather than a proven Docker pull failure.

FIX-B (pin verification): pip list non-empty gate passed vacuously with only 'pip 26.2.1' (pip freeze empty, sha256 e3b0c442... — reproduced in audit environment). The frozen intent was BrowserGym-core 0.14.3 / AgentLab 0.4.2 / Playwright 1.63.0 / tiktoken present. None are installed (M_SUBSTRATE_PLAYWRIGHT/BROWSERGYM/WEBGYM false all confirmed). Install the pinned stack on the runner BEFORE the capture attempt or the H1/H2 branches are untenable regardless of Docker.

FIX-C (within-family sampling determinism): family-level draw random.Random(35725763380).sample(sorted(families_ge3_id),10) recomputes exactly to producer's [191,180,162,197,153,213,163,137,136,222] (MATCH). But within-family task selection uses random.Random(SEED + hash(str(fid)) % 100000) (run script line 248); hash() on str is PYTHONHASHSEED-salted per process. Audit ran 4 fresh processes: family 222 produced task pairs [24,25], [23,24], [25,22], [23,25] and family 191 produced [798,795], [797,798], [798,797] — none reproducibly equal to the recorded [23,25] / [798,797] except by chance. Replace hash(str(fid)) with a deterministic derivation (e.g., int(sha256(str(fid))[:8],16) or the raw numeric family id) so recorded sampled_tasks re-derive from seed 35725763380 in any process, satisfying prereg 'Frozen seed ... for ALL choices'.

FIX-D (frozen grammar completeness): grammar_fulltree_358885.py sha256 74ab5a2b... (recorded as the frozen representation identity) contains the 9 base regexes and 6 Magento patterns but NO body regex (has_body_regex false, confirmed by file read). CRITICAL FIX 1 requires body regex before outerHTML SHA256. The run script simulates a body strip at capture time (lines 317-321) but that is not part of the grammar module whose hash is recorded; a substrate-live run with grammar hash 74ab5a2b would not satisfy the frozen normalization. Add the body regex to grammar_fulltree_358885.py and record the new live hash, or the H1 representation remains non-frozen.

FIX-F (design-level, for Director/next DESIGN — cannot be fixed inside EXECUTE): of the 10 frozen-drawn families, only 2 (136, 222) have sampled tasks whose start URLs are product pages (verified from webarena-verified.json start_urls and ax_captures.jsonl expansions); the other 8 sampled tasks start at the __SHOPPING__ root (order details, contact form, category listing, coupon request). Parent handoff established only 4 product-page families are live (222,136,145,196) and shopping_admin 404s. Even with a fully live substrate, this draw yields at most 2 product-page families / 4 product trees, failing the frozen >=10 product-page families adequacy gate (and the 'product-subtree distinct SHA on 136/145/196/222' check is incomputable since 145/196 are not in the draw). H1 as frozen cannot reach SURVIVES/FALSIFIED with this sampling base; amend the sample to draw only product-page-capable tasks (or resolve shopping_admin 404) before the next substrate-live attempt, else the MEASUREMENT_INVALID streak continues for reasons unrelated to substrate.

V2 (HIGH — 'environment limit 8s' misattribution): result.json validity_notes 'CRITICAL HOST LIMITATION: ... environment limited to 8s per command' and report.md §5 'environment enforces 8s command timeout' attribute the Docker timeout to the host. Raw evidence (webarena_verified_pin.json docker_pull/run entries + script code) shows the 8s/5s limits were passed by the measurement script itself (run_cmd timeout=8 / timeout=5), and the raised exception is Python subprocess.TimeoutExpired from that parameter. Audit environment check `timeout 8 sleep 12; echo $?` → 124 (timeout tool) but plain `sleep 12` → completes: no 8s host cap is evident. The 'falsifier clause met' statement in result.json validity_notes overstates compliance (1 registry API attempt, not 3; pulls at 8s, not >=300s; no docker load/ghcr mirror). Classification remains conservatively correct because the browser stack is absent regardless, but the rationale as written is not supported by evidence.

The within-family task-pair selection (2 distinct tasks per family) is NOT reproducible across processes because of hash() salting (FIX-C). Since 0 captures occurred, no measured metric is affected this run, but the recorded sampled_tasks cannot be re-derived from the seed, violating the frozen all-choices determinism requirement.
